trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (trimmed_mean on pool1) and the runner-up margin is statistically indistinguishable. The series has unstable ranking (Kendall tau 0.072), high error correlation (0.836), and only 3 validation windows making weight estimation high-variance. The trimmed mean over the 5 most stable models already captures the robust combination the diagnosis calls for, and further tuning is unlikely to produce a real gain over noise.

action_args.justification: The series is stationary with moderate seasonality and no trend, but model ranking is highly unstable (Kendall tau 0.072) and errors are strongly correlated (mean 0.836, only 2 independent groups). With only 3 validation windows, fitted weights are high-variance. The trimmed mean over the 5 most consistently-ranked models (spanning the ETS/THETA, DWT, and FT error groups) provides robustness against both the unstable ranking and the occasional outlier model, while the 20% trim guards against the worst-performing member in any given window. The runner-up (plain mean on the same pool) is statistically indistinguishable, confirming that the robust combination is the right kind of strategy for this noisy, moderately predictable series.
